Comments: Mandatory data breach notification requirements could not be confirmed in enacted law; sources referenced only a draft Data Protection Bill (not enacted) that would require breach reporting/notification.[ITLawCo – Namibia Data Protection Bill](https://itlawco.com/focus-areas/data-protection-and-privacy/namibias-data-protection-bill-moving-towards-privacy-and-data-security/)

revised_comments: Bank of Namibia Determination PSD-12 (Determination of the Operational and Cybersecurity Standards within the National Payment System), effective 1 July 2023, imposes mandatory breach notification obligations on National Payment System participants. Successful cyberattack incidents must be reported to the Bank of Namibia within 24 hours of detection, with a full impact assessment covering financial loss, data loss and availability loss required within one month. The obligation applies to payment system operators and payment service providers regulated under the Payment System Management Act.

Comments: No public independent audit reports of the national payment systems (NamPay/IPN) were located. BoN PSD-6 requires payment system operators to submit audited financial statements to BoN (regulatory requirement), but this is not the same as publicly available audits.[BoN PSD-6 (Gov Gazette No. 8382)](https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2024/8382.pdf)

revision_notes: Light check surfaced a directly relevant primary source, escalating this row to full verification. Fetched and read Bank of Namibia Determination PSD-1 ('Licensing and Authorisation of Payment Service Providers in Namibia', effective 15 February 2024), Part VI paragraph 15.1, which requires non-bank financial institution payment service providers to submit annual audited financial statements, signed off by a reputable independent auditor, within three months of financial year-end. This confirms independent third-party audits are mandated by regulation, but there is no evidence the results are made public — the joint Bank of Namibia/NAMFISA Financial Stability Report discusses payment system risk in aggregate but does not disclose individual operator audit findings. Score raised from 0 (Unknown) to 2 (Private Audits). Note the original comment's reference to 'PSD-6' appears to be a citation error; the applicable determination is PSD-1 (Gov Gazette No. 8308).
revised_comments: Bank of Namibia Determination PSD-1 (Licensing and Authorisation of Payment Service Providers in Namibia), effective 15 February 2024, requires non-bank financial institution payment service providers to submit annual audited financial statements, signed off by a reputable independent auditor, within three months of their financial year-end. Independent third-party audits of payment service providers are therefore mandated by regulation, but results are submitted to the regulator rather than published; the Bank of Namibia and NAMFISA jointly publish an annual Financial Stability Report discussing payment system risk at an aggregate level, without disclosing individual audit findings.

Comments: Government payment digitization share could not be quantified from available sources; evidence indicates G2P digitization is in pilot/UAT phase for social grants/pensions rather than majority of government payments.[New Era](https://neweralive.na/namibia-draws-closer-to-instant-government-payments/)

revision_notes: Light check surfaced substantive, dated evidence beyond the original pilot/UAT reference, escalating this row to full verification. Fetched the Instant Payment Namibia (IPN) fact sheet and corroborating news reports (TechNews and New Era, 17-19 June 2026), which confirm that Namibia's Instant Payment Solution went live for its first Government-to-Person (G2P) use case on 17 June 2026, disbursing grants to a single category ('Marginalised Beneficiaries') through one participating bank (Bank Windhoek), described as a 'controlled go-live' within a phased rollout; a second institution (Letshego Bank Namibia) has since completed G2P certification, but wider rollout across all government payment types (salaries, pensions, other grant categories) had not occurred as of the source date. This indicates government payment digitisation via the instant payment system is in its earliest phase, well under 20% of total government payments. Score raised from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (<20%).
revised_comments: Namibia's government payment digitisation via the national Instant Payment Solution (IPS/IPN) is at an early, pilot stage. The first live Government-to-Person (G2P) payments were processed on 17 June 2026, disbursing grants to beneficiaries in the 'Marginalised Beneficiaries' category through Bank Windhoek, with Letshego Bank Namibia also certified for the G2P phase shortly after. This represents a controlled go-live within Phase 1 of a phased rollout plan; broader government payment types, including salaries, pensions and other social grant categories, have not yet migrated to the instant payment system, placing digitisation of government payments via this channel well below 20% of total government disbursements.
